topic: Secondary-vote majority-sign classification—overlapping nominal code false reversals
A_question: Can non-disjoint secondary nominal codes induce a STRICT_REVERSAL classification even though each named code appears on two opposing options? Correct behavior should fail closed or explicitly mark malformed rather than report reversal.

B_competitors.H1: Existing compare_ballot simply counts whitespace tokens per option; duplicates across S/N allow synthetic spurious strict reversal
B_competitors.H0: Existing code prevents overlapping codes, so no spurious reversal
B_competitors.alternative: The source itself does not promise code disjointness, so tests can only strengthen an invariant—not authenticate the original vote.

other_negative_controls: Duplicated code within one option must also be rejected
Malformed totals should be rejected without classifying reversal
Unknown nominal option should not be silently counted into n_any

D_execution_contract: Reconstruct exact source bytes from connector and verify Git blob SHA in Linux sandbox (no external network)
Execute original tests with pytest when available; preserve first red failing case
If H1 observed, implement minimal fail-closed input guard and add regression tests
Re-run full local targeted test file; do not claim global suite
Hash new sources and independently compare to GitHub after commit
F: Examine whether duplicate code uses alternate labels, whitespace, booleans, missing/extra groups; ensure no unverified official inference
G: Local code-level replication with original source matching Git blob and targeted tests only
H: No scientific discovery/N1-3 uplift from synthetic fixtures
I: product/method data hygiene, not issuer semantics or real vote certification
J: STOP_R5 if inputs already validated; otherwise repair targeted false classifications, freeze tests
safety: Synthetic codes only; never publish names or personal votes, no CI, no Codex, no real scoring
